We see no reason to say that the Mu'tazilites borrowed this principle from Aristotle's idea of the golden mean — Aristotle held that virtue was the middle ground between excess and deficiency. The Quran itself abounds in verses commending moderation and the middle course, such as God's words: “And so We have made you a community of the middle way, so that you may bear witness before humanity.” And His words: “Do not pray too loudly or too quietly, but seek a way between the two.” ↩
